channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Astana to Invest Around 40 Billion Tenge in Investment Projects
item.description: Approximately 40 billion tenge are planned for investment in Astana's development projects. This funding aims to stimulate economic growth and infrastructure development within the capital city.

item.title: KMF Bank Adapts to New Banking Landscape, Focuses on Digital and Human Services
item.description: KMF Bank has transformed to meet banking standards, enhancing risk management and corporate governance. It now offers current accounts, deposits, payment cards, and digital services. The bank aims to provide comprehensive financial solutions, particularly for entrepreneurs, blending digital convenience with expert advice.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Major Privatization Program, Offering Assets Worth Over $8 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan has initiated a large-scale privatization program, putting state-owned assets valued at over $8 billion up for sale. The initiative includes stakes in companies, banks, and the national airline, aiming to attract investment for modernization. Experts caution about potential corruption risks.

item.title: Kazakhstan to analyze state governance mechanisms for improvement
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has emphasized the need for fundamental economic reform alongside political changes. Digitalization is seen as key to economic efficiency and competitiveness. The government will review tax and budget codes, with potential amendments to the tax code if certain norms negatively impact entrepreneurship. A strategic plan for improving state governance is due by June 1.

item.title: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway: 22% of construction to be completed by end of 2026
item.description: Construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is planned to reach 22% of the total work volume by the end of 2026. According to Ulan Kulov, deputy general director of the railway company, work is underway on 11 sections of the Kyrgyz part of the route. Tunneling is 21.5% complete, bridge foundations 95% complete, and earthworks 67% complete. Over 10,000 people are currently involved in construction.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President addresses business concerns regarding new tax code
item.description: Kazakhstan's President emphasized the need to support entrepreneurship, calling illegal barriers against business a crime against the state. While violations by SMEs decreased, fines increased, prompting a review of state control methods. The President has tasked the government with considering a three-year moratorium on inspections for SMEs starting January 1 and urged the government to heed business feedback on the tax code, making necessary amendments.

item.title: Russia: European nations not invited to trilateral Ukraine talks
item.description: Russia plans to resume trilateral negotiations on Ukraine involving Russia, the United States, and Ukraine. However, European Union representatives will not be invited to these talks, according to Yuri Ushakov, an aide to the Russian president. The discussion of these trilateral talks between the US, Russia, and Ukraine was previously discussed during a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US special envoy Steve Witkoff.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Delivers Address to the Nation on New Historical Stage
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has published his traditional address to the people of Kazakhstan, titled 'Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era.' The address follows recent national celebrations, including Republic Day and the adoption of the Constitution, marking significant political and institutional reforms.

item.title: Entrepreneur to build cascade of hydropower plants in Turkistan region
item.description: A cascade of water pipelines with a capacity of 72 MW will be built in the Turkistan region, supplying water to several settlements. The Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation and 'South Hydro Power' LLP signed an agreement for the project. This initiative will provide quality drinking water to over 1 million residents and reduce the region's energy deficit by generating 72 MW of green electricity annually.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans Three-Year Moratorium for Small and Micro Businesses Starting 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan is planning to introduce a three-year moratorium on inspections for small and micro businesses starting January 1, 2027. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed this initiative, aiming to ease the burden on entrepreneurs. This follows a previous moratorium that was extended until early 2024.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees More Job Losses Than Hires in First Half of 2026
item.description: In the first half of 2026, Kazakhstan hired 268,400 employees, an increase of 10.8% year-on-year. However, 278,700 people left their jobs, an 8% increase, resulting in 10,300 more dismissals than new hires. This contrasts with Kyrgyzstan, where hirings exceeded departures.

item.title: Kazakh Parliament Ratifies Protocol Amending Eurasian Economic Union Treaty
item.description: The Parliament of Kazakhstan has ratified a protocol introducing amendments to the treaty on the Eurasian Economic Union. The ratification occurred during a session where the Chairman of the Kurultai, Aybek Dadebay, outlined tasks related to the President's Address on Kazakhstan's priorities in a new historical period.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Experts Predict Potential Dollar Rise to 500 Tenge Amidst Tenge Strengthening
item.description: Despite the tenge's recent strengthening, analysts foresee a possible rise in the US dollar's value, potentially reaching 500 tenge within the next year. Factors contributing to the tenge's appreciation include high oil prices and increased foreign investment. Experts advise caution and suggest that significant currency fluctuations primarily impact large-scale investors.

item.title: Eurasian Development Bank Forecasts Kazakhstan's Economy to Grow by 5% This Year
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank projects Kazakhstan's economy to grow by nearly 5% this year, with similar growth expected next year. However, growth may slow to 4.1-4.2% by 2028-2029. Non-oil sectors and new projects are driving growth, despite challenges in oil production and Caspian Pipeline Consortium repairs. Inflation is expected to reach 9.5% by year-end.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Build Cascade of Hydropower Plants and Water Pipeline in Turkestan Region
item.description: A company linked to a Forbes-listed businessman will construct a 72 MW hydropower cascade and a 54.7 km water pipeline on the Ugam River in the Turkestan Region. The project, signed by the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation and South Hydro Power LLP, aims to provide quality drinking water to over 1 million residents and reduce the region's energy deficit. The agreement outlines water consumption volumes and project phases.

item.title: Foreign Ministers of Tajikistan and Pakistan Hold Phone Conversation
item.description: On October 28, 2026, at the initiative of the Pakistani side, the Foreign Minister of Tajikistan, Sirojiddin Mukhriddin, held a phone conversation with the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan, Ishaq Dar. The parties discussed the current state of bilateral cooperation and prospects for its further development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry Denies Reports of Attack on Politician Adakhan Madumarov
item.description: The Ministry of Internal Affairs of Kyrgyzstan has refuted information circulating on social media alleging an attack on politician Adakhan Madumarov. The ministry confirmed it investigated the claims and found them to be unsubstantiated, urging citizens to rely on official sources and avoid spreading unverified information.

item.title: US Imposes Sanctions on Two Russians Linked to North Korean IT Scams
item.description: The U.S. Treasury Department has sanctioned ten individuals and one entity for their alleged involvement in North Korean IT fraud schemes. Among those sanctioned are two Russian citizens, Vitold Obertas and Ilya Boykov, along with eight North Korean nationals. The U.S. claims North Korean IT specialists used fraudulent documents and stolen data to secure jobs at foreign companies, with profits funding weapons programs.

item.title: Rain and Mudflows Expected in Parts of Tajikistan on October 29-30
item.description: The Tajikistan Hydrometeorological Agency has announced unfavorable weather conditions for October 29 and 30, with rain expected in several regions. This increases the risk of mudflows in foothill and mountainous areas of Sughd, republican subordinate regions, and Darvaz district of GBAO. Citizens are advised to take precautions.

item.title: Moldovan President Convenes Security Council Amidst Large-Scale Cyberattack
item.description: Moldovan President Maia Sandu has called a meeting of the Security Council due to a significant cyberattack targeting the country. Authorities reported approximately 11 million requests to state services, with attackers attempting to extract information between October 19-23. Personal data of up to 750,000 citizens may have been compromised. State services are still not fully restored.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Seeks Larger Fuel Shipments from Russia, Say Oil Traders
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's oil traders are seeking to receive larger volumes of fuel and lubricants from Russia. While supplies continue, the association of oil traders indicated a desire for increased quantities. Companies are also diversifying imports from countries like Belarus, Turkey, and Italy. Rising global fuel prices are attributed to the geopolitical situation in the Middle East.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Fuel Prices to Rise Without Government Subsidies, Warns Traders
item.description: The Association of Oil Traders in Kyrgyzstan warns that fuel prices will inevitably increase if the government stops subsidizing fuel imports. Head Kanatbek Eshanov stated that without state support, traders would operate on market terms, leading to higher prices, similar to Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Offers Condolences for Deadly Train Collision in Spain
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has sent condolences to the King of Spain following a collision between two trains in the province of Toledo. The accident resulted in 64 fatalities and over 170 injuries. The trains were traveling from Madrid to Seville when one rear-ended the other. Rescue and recovery operations are ongoing.

item.title: US War Spending Against Iran Surpasses $47 Billion, Exceeding Pentagon's July Estimate
item.description: US expenditures on the war with Iran have exceeded $47 billion, a figure over 25% higher than the Pentagon's July estimate. These costs include operational expenses for warfare, flight operations, and cyber support, with projected costs for replenishing munitions exceeding $29 billion. Further expenses are anticipated for replacing lost military equipment and repairing damaged US bases.

item.title: Uzbek President to Attend Turkic States Summit in Ankara
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Turkey from October 29-30 to participate in the upcoming summit of the Organization of Turkic States in Ankara. The summit, themed 'Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Deed,' will focus on strengthening cooperation in trade, economy, transport, culture, tourism, ecology, and education.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Boost Economic Ties Through Regional and Business Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia are strengthening economic cooperation through increased trade, industrial projects, and direct regional and business ties. Bilateral trade reached $13 billion in 2025, an 8.4% increase. Upcoming events like 'AgroExpo Uzbekistan 2026' aim to foster new business connections and explore new cooperation avenues.

item.title: Over Two Kilograms of Powdered Drug Seized from Suspected Courier in Almaty
item.description: A 25-year-old man suspected of working as a drug courier was detained in Almaty's Nauryzbai district. Police found over a kilogram of suspected mephedrone in a car-sharing vehicle and approximately another kilogram at his residence. Additional hashish weighing about 50 grams was also seized. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Caspian States Convene in Ashgabat to Advance Marine Scientific Research Cooperation
item.description: Turkmenistan hosted a meeting of Caspian Sea littoral states in Ashgabat to discuss cooperation on marine scientific research. Delegates reviewed a draft agreement aimed at facilitating research in the Caspian Sea, where countries aim to develop oil and gas reserves while addressing environmental concerns. The initiative was first proposed in 2018.

item.title: Uzbekistan's New Tashkent Attracts Investors with Favorable Conditions
item.description: An investor shares positive experiences in Uzbekistan's New Tashkent, citing favorable conditions and implemented projects. Despite initial skepticism, Russian entrepreneur Alexander Bakanov has launched four major projects, praising the business environment. The initiative aims to attract $50 billion in investments for projects on a 6,000-hectare area.

item.title: German Publication 'Welt' Highlights Uzbekistan's Cultural Opening to the World
item.description: The German publication 'Welt' notes Uzbekistan's efforts in developing culture, preserving heritage, and promoting national values internationally. The article highlights the growing global interest in Uzbekistan's culture, citing a concert by Lang Lang in Samarkand as an example of its cultural reforms and international engagement.

item.title: Tokayev's Niece Heads New Parliamentary Group 'Children of Kazakhstan'
item.description: Dana Medeuova, niece of President Tokayev, has been appointed head of the new parliamentary group 'Children of Kazakhstan'. The group aims to unite parliamentary efforts to address child protection issues. Medeuova emphasized that child rights are a state policy priority, with a focus on digital safety and equal educational opportunities.

item.title: Taliban-Pakistan Border Clash in Torkham Leaves One Child Dead, Two Aid Workers Injured
item.description: A clash between Taliban forces and Pakistani military personnel in Torkham resulted in the death of one child and injuries to two aid workers. The incident, which began on Wednesday evening, caused a temporary halt to the return of refugees to Afghanistan. Tensions remain high at the border.

item.title: Protest Held in Istanbul After Death of Kazakh Woman
item.description: Activists from the "Socialist Women's Councils" (SKM) protested in Istanbul where a 26-year-old Kazakh woman, Aisulu Bekmakhanova, died. They called her death suspicious, rejecting explanations of suicide or falling. The protest, part of preparations for the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, featured slogans like 'This is not suicide, it is murder.'

item.title: Thailand Plans 15-Day Visa-Free Regime for Uzbek Citizens
item.description: Thailand is planning to introduce a 15-day visa-free regime for citizens of Uzbekistan. This news digest also includes information on the World Bank allocating $100 million for modernizing Uzbekistan's power grids, Shavkat Mirziyoyev's greetings to participants of the Central Asia International Education Forum, and expected weather changes in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Cultural Ties with Leading French Institutions
item.description: Uzbekistan's Fund for Cultural Development and Art is strengthening international cooperation and preparing for the 2027 Bukhara Biennale. Meetings with Centre Pompidou leadership resulted in a cooperation agreement for long-term partnership and a future exhibition showcasing Uzbek art. Discussions also took place at Lafayette Anticipations and Fondation Cartier for the upcoming biennale.

item.title: Uzbek Education Minister Highlights Future Impact of Educational Decisions
item.description: Decisions made in education today shape future economic development and opportunities, according to Uzbek Minister of Education and Science Erkin Turdimov at the Central Asia International Education Forum in Tashkent. He stressed the importance of regional cooperation for practical results, improving learning quality, and unlocking youth potential in a rapidly changing global economy.

item.title: Ecologists Explain Cause of Air Pollution in Tashkent
item.description: Ecologists have explained the cause of air pollution in Tashkent. Windless weather and temperature inversions observed in Central Asia during October led to the accumulation of harmful particles in the atmosphere. The article provides further details on the phenomenon.

item.title: Germany Deports 40 Criminal Migrants to Afghanistan
item.description: Germany's Interior Ministry confirmed the deportation of 40 "criminal migrants" to Afghanistan. The individuals, including those convicted of sexual offenses, violence, and drug trafficking, were reportedly sent directly from prison. Germany has increased such deportations following an agreement with the Taliban, while human rights groups and UN experts express concerns.

item.title: Uzbek Citizens Face Increased Scrutiny at Foreign Borders Amidst New Entry Rules
item.description: Uzbek citizens are experiencing heightened checks at international borders, with countries like Thailand, Montenegro, and Egypt implementing new entry regulations. Some Uzbeks are being denied entry and turned back. This trend raises questions about why Uzbeks are becoming 'unwanted' guests as Uzbekistan opens up to the world.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Begins Receiving Fuel Shipments from China via Railway
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has started receiving fuel and lubricants from China via railway, according to Kanatbek Eshatov, president of the Oil Traders Association. While fuel imports previously came mainly from Russia, Kyrgyzstan now sources them from Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan, Belarus, and Turkey. The country is experiencing a slight gasoline deficit and seeking diverse suppliers.
